scope: Complete the same existing Lando lead. No fourth source, final asset acquisition, page implementation, packaging, publication or seven-dimension admission.

verification.actualViewing: All 141 source frames were actually viewed in this agent context: normal53 in five labelled contact sheets, inputs38 in four, path-details44 in four, gallery6 as full images. Their source bytes were reverified unchanged now; recommended states were also inspected full size. This is observation, not an independent calibrated review.
verification.browserRecovery: Before capture on 2026-10-31 00:37 local, old PID21648 and port1110 were absent. Only then a new isolated session webart-007-lando-20261031 was created. Old 72-frame scout and failed supplement were preserved.

opening.finding: Stable default shows a specific frontal portrait with spatially fitted transparent helmet wireframe. Continuous mouse paths reveal black reflective visor and decorated helmet bands at the corresponding face location; after leave/stop those bands decay. The signature changes the visible identity between person and racing equipment, rather than just moving an image.
opening.mechanismEvidence: Visible fullscreen canvas.gl has data-engine three.js r174. Browser resource metadata records already loaded helmet-21.glb, disco-02.glb, tracks-06-test.glb and HDR environment names; no model, shader or site code was separately requested or copied. This establishes a real Three.js helmet layer and does not establish that the human portrait is a separate 3D head mesh.
opening.desktopNormalAndReduced: Both actual media preferences show visor/helmet bands moving with the continuous native pointer trace, with idle, leave and reentry observations. Single slow point-moves mostly allowed the trail to decay; the continuous sequence supplies the actual coupled-effect evidence.
opening.phoneNormalAndReduced: Actual short tap near the observed lower-right control followed by held finger x80→310→80 at y450 reveals the visor band at successive face positions. UI changes to BACK TO SCROLL/X during interaction and returns after the final tap. This proves the finger-controlled band and usable return, not a complete full-helmet paint or a precise attribution of the earlier UI transition to one tap.
unproven: The bounded NEXT RACE point-hover did not demonstrate a complete helmet pull-on; do not use those filenames as proof.
A generic static photo mask or a replacement 3D human head is not established by these observations.

path.finding: Forward path actually goes from portrait to reduced portrait/signature, dark legacy statement, staggered life/racing photography with dark-to-light transition, opposed profile/helmet composition, close person-and-helmet photograph, varied helmet collection, store/partners/social fan and a separately designed portrait-with-helmet closing.
path.reducedMotionLimit: Reduced preference was truly set before navigation. Same hero input, full forward end, extra input and one reverse/stop were captured on both widths. Source still animates; this is not a claim of stopped rendering, source performance compliance or a full reduced reverse to opening.

collection.finding: Observed collection cards use paired base/hover WebP images. Native desktop hover on the first Season2025 card replaces the isolated helmet render with a photograph of that same helmet worn by the same person, with border/image treatment; leaving restores the base. Moving within this card changes the crop treatment, not a proven freely rotatable 3D collection object.
collection.desktopClick: First-card click left the same URL and no dialog. Its image result matched the hover state; no separate detail page or full collection interaction was established.
collection.phoneTap: First-card native taps in normal and reduced motion left the same visible base helmet, same URL and no dialog. Phone photographic hover replacement is not proven; do not mark it passed.
collection.loadingLimit: desktop-gallery-first-hover had complete=false while the photo was still arriving. desktop-gallery-first-move and first-click were complete=true with the finished photograph; use these as stable hover evidence and retain the early frame as an honest load transition.
collection.notEstablished: No evidence that every collection card requires its own realtime model or opens separate details. Do not remove the collection or its product-to-use identity to reduce asset work.

ending.finding: Actual finite closing uses an irregular dark-green frame, signature/type composition and the same patterned torso wearing the complete helmet; phone rearranges links above the centered subject. This is a specific media composition, not only contact tools.
ending.limits: Late logo-strip movement is ambient. Left/right ending pointer screenshots did not establish a new head-rotation signature. Phone metadata includes a visible pre-rendered portrait/helmet cutout image; do not infer that every closing pixel requires realtime 3D.

required: A mature explicitly redistributable helmet model/material set with convincing visor, thickness and highlights, accurately fitted to a legally usable person/portrait; do not substitute a primitive or ordinary masked image for the spatial helmet.
A coherent person/outfit/product image set across hero, life/racing story, profile comparison, contextual gallery photos and closing, or an explicitly reviewed replacement identity plan.
Varied finished collection designs and their contextual appearance must be supported by permitted media. Model names suggested by the chief are leads, not adopted or license-cleared assets.
replacementFeasibility.notRequiredByEvidence: The current observation does not require fabricating a new human-head mesh or sixteen realtime helmet models. Neither simplification nor those extra requirements should be silently inferred.
